title: structured output: add CFG + regex constrained decoding backends and tokenizer edgecase handling
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: We need robust structured-output constrained decoding that works across backends (sampling, beam, streaming) and handles real-world tokenizer edgecases (unicode, surrogate pairs, mixed-tokenizer artifacts). Existing constrained-decoding code covered basic CFG-style constraints at the token-id level but failed on regex constraints where tokenization split pattern boundaries and produced incorrect accept/reject decisions. This PR: 1) Introduces a backend-agnostic constrained-decoding interface and two concrete backends: a CFG-compiled backend and a token-aware regex backend. 2) Adds a tokenizer compatibility layer that normalizes inputs for regex constraints, performs token-to-byte mapping fallbacks for languages with complex unicode, and exposes a small set of tokenizer invariants used by the constraint engines. 3) Improves streaming stability: constraints can now be applied mid-stream with incremental state snapshots and graceful fallback when partial tokens are emitted from the tokenizer. 4) Adds extensive unit and integration tests (including fuzz tests) and microbenchmarks to validate perf/regressions. Backward compatibility: default decoder behavior is unchanged; new backends are opt-in via the constrained_decoding.backend config. Notes on changes: - CFG backend compiles grammars to a compact deterministic state machine that operates on token-ids and supports lookahead and optional tokens. - Regex backend uses a token-aware regex engine: we compile regexes against normalized token sequences and fall back to a byte-level regex when token-boundaries would otherwise break the match. - Tokenizer fixes: normalize NFKC for regex constraints, treat surrogate pairs as single token spans for regex matching, and add an escaped-byte fallback for models that use byte-level BPE. - Streaming: added an incremental checkpoint API and a rule to delay acceptance until token emission boundary is stable (configurable). - Performance: added hot-path optimizations (caching compiled constraints, lazy-lookahead, and compact DFA representation) and microbenchmarks showing <5% throughput regression for most workloads, with large gains on constrained-heavy prompts. Checklist: - [x] Backend interface and implementations - [x] Tokenizer compatibility layer - [x] Unit tests + fuzz harness - [x] Integration tests (streaming + batch) - [x] Perf microbenchmarks - [x] Docs updates (developer guide + config reference) See linked linear items for rollout plan and telemetry to measure feature adoption and perf impact.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: This looks great overall. A few perf questions: can you avoid copying token arrays on every regex check? Also add a small benchmark comparing compiled DFA vs on-the-fly regex for common short grammars.
Asha Patel: Responded - switched to view slices with shared buffers for hot-paths and added the microbenchmark in perf/microbenchmarks. See commit e6f8b32.

Samir Gupta: Found a failure on Japanese surrogate pairs in the fuzz harness - regex backend rejected valid matches where tokens split in the middle. Please add normalization and a byte-fallback path.
Asha Patel: Added NFKC normalization and token-to-byte fallback in tokenizer/compat.py; updated tests. See commit d47a0ea.
Lina Chen: One nit: add logging hook when falling back to byte-level regex so we can track frequency in prod. Also ensure the extra logs are debug-level only.
Asha Patel: Added debug-level fallback logging and an opt-in telemetry flag. Pushed changes.
Lina Chen: Approving. Verified CI and perf numbers look acceptable. Will squash-merge after final CI pass.
CI Bot: One flaky integration test (streaming_constraints::test_partial_token_acceptance) failed on first run; rerun passed. All checks green.
merge_outcome: merged by Lina Chen via squash and merge. Rollout: staged on dedicated clusters for 48h with telemetry enabled, then full rollout. Release notes: Added CFG and token-aware regex constrained-decoding backends; tokenizer normalizations for regex constraints; streaming stability improvements; opt-in via constrained_decoding.backend. No breaking changes by default.
release_notes: Added CFG and token-aware regex constrained-decoding backends; tokenizer NFKC normalization and surrogate-pair handling for regex constraints; streaming checkpointing for mid-stream constraint application; opt-in via config. Performance: <5% median throughput regression in most workloads; large improvements on constrained-heavy prompts.
notes_for_ops: Enable constrained_decoding.telemetry to collect fallback counts and perf metrics during staged rollout. Watch constrained_backends.dfa_cache.hit_rate and constrained_backends.regex.fallback_rate. If fallback_rate > 1% for a customer, consider enabling tokenizer.byte_fallback per-model.
